BiblicalUsage: In Aramaic this word is an arm, and by figure it means force or power, and it occurs once in Ezra. When the king's letter arrives, the enemies of Judah go up to Jerusalem in haste and make them stop building by force and power. One word carries the whole threat: the king's arm against God's house.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe no arm of man can stop what God has commanded to be built, because the temple rose again despite the force sent against it.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile
